newsitem.title: USA: Belgium's Maystadt says EMU will launch on time.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Maystadt says EMU will launch on time.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt insisted Thursday that European monetary union would take place on schedule.
"European monetary union will come -- will come -- on Jan. 1, 1999," Maystadt told an Atlanta luncheon meeting sponsored by the Belgian-American Chamber of Commerce.
Maystadt said skepticism in the United States over implementation of EMU is understandable, but he told his audience they should believe it will happen.
Maystadt said establishment of the euro is a natural outgrowth of the European Common Market.
"Given time, Europe would unite with one currency," he said.
Maystadt said the euro's function will spread beyond its role within the EMU in that non-members would peg their money to the new currency.
"I'm quite sure the euro will be a transition currency not only for member states but also for central and eastern (European) countries," he said.
Maystadt said those countries' currencies were already anchored by the German mark and would be pegged to the euro after the EMU began operating.
